summary: Onslow County survey mark FIRE TOWER 2 (EA2358): a 1950 NGS description of a 135-foot green steel skeleton tower; last recovered in 2003 in good condition.

facts.design: Steel skeleton tower, painted green (1950 description)
facts.status_note: No source says whether the tower still stands. The last recovery, in 2003, found the survey station in good condition.

notes_for_editor: The NGS datasheet is the only source for the 1950 description and the 1993 and 2003 recoveries. It describes the survey station and its tower but does not say who built the tower, when it went up, or what it was used for. The word 'fire' appears only in the mark's name and in the tnlandforms list title, so the fire-lookout link rests on the name. The datasheet's coordinates sit about 12 m from the tnlandforms point (our calculation). No register, Forest Service or newspaper source was found. A lejeune.marines.mil article on Camp Lejeune fire towers returned HTTP 403, and a Waymarking Lejeune Fire Tower page returned no text; that waymark is for the Lejeune tower at 34.61083, -77.28972 on the tnlandforms list, not this site. Three WebSearch calls were made for this tower, one more than the two-call budget. The register field keeps NGS EA 2358, matching the other records.
